description: Reports of the engineers (sub-agents, decision D-023) who wrote and later maintained the test suites and the check tools without having written the code under test: what they wrote, what they found, and what was done about each defect (resolution: fix / record / decline, with a note by the coordinator).  Reports are verbatim except that local paths of the build machine are shortened.  The first-generation authors left 53 tests failing on purpose, each documenting a defect.  49 of them exist under the same name and pass in the gate run.  4 no longer exist under that name: three were replaced by the maintainers with tests of the rule that took their place (see tests_removed in the maintenance reports: request and report at the same instant, the outdated position snapshot handed to the gateway, the run context without a clock), and one - the bounds of the last representable trading day - was rewritten by the coordinator to the documented inclusive bound.

reports.author: contracts_compatibility

defects_found.description: The evolution check rejects the framework's own way of adding a field. A field declared with fld(Opt(...), since=(1, n)) makes object_schema() publish 'x-gie-since'. classify_schema_change treats the appearance of that keyword, and any later growth of the map, as 'keyword added or removed' and returns MAJOR. Section 8 says a new optional field is MINOR, so schema_gen --check would refuse the first legitimate 1.1.0 of any contract.
defects_found.resolution_note: corrected in the second rework (reviews/session_00/rework_2_change_notice.md); the tests that documented it pass in the gate run

defects_found.description: OrderEvent has two ranks inside one stream, so ordering_key is not monotonic in seq. When a broker report has the same receive instant as the request it answers (normal in zero-latency replay, where virtual time does not advance while code runs), the report (rank 20, seq n+1) sorts before the request (rank 80, seq n). validate_order_transition and MemoryJournal.publish accept the sequence, but the key order contradicts stream order, the 'causal fallback' of section 6.2 is not causal for request -> report, and merge_ordered raises OutOfOrderError for the stream. This needs a coordinator decision: either require a report to be strictly later than its request, or change the rank scheme or the documented claim.
defects_found.file: gie/contracts/ordering.py (STREAMS / ordering_key; table in SHARED_CONTRACTS.md section 6.1)
defects_found.reproducer:
from tests.gie import samples; from tests.gie.samples import T0
from gie.contracts import OrderEventType, OrderState, identity, ordering_key, validate_order_transition
req = samples.order_event(event_time_ns=T0, receive_time_ns=T0)
rep = samples.order_event(seq=1, order_seq=1, event_type=OrderEventType.ACCEPTED, order_state=OrderState.WORKING, event_time_ns=T0, receive_time_ns=T0, broker_order_id=identity.broker_order_id(req.client_order_id))
validate_order_transition(req, rep)  # accepted
ordering_key(req) < ordering_key(rep)  # False: (T0, 80, s, 0) vs (T0, 20, s, 1)
defects_found.resolution_note: EventKey is the input-order key of a run: a broker report is an input (rank 20), a request is one of GIE's own records (rank 80).  It is therefore not monotonic in seq within an order-event stream and is not meant to be; the order of a stream is seq and the order of a run is the journal.  Stated in specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md 6.1 / 6.2; in addition a report is now strictly later than the request it answers (validate_order_transition).

defects_found.description: The routing-lock rule in classify_schema_change only fires when an existing properties.mode / properties.venue enum changes. A contract that gains a new optional mode or venue field whose vocabulary contains LIVE is classified MINOR ('new optional field'). Section 8 says any change of the run-mode or venue vocabulary is MAJOR. The independent check routing_vocabulary_problems() in schema_gen.check() still reports this case (covered by a passing test), so the lock holds; only the classification is wrong.

defects_found.description: market_event_id lets non-GieError exceptions escape for invalid Decimal prices. sorted(set(prices)) runs before any finiteness check, so a NaN next to another price raises decimal.InvalidOperation and a signalling NaN raises TypeError. A single NaN or an infinity correctly gives CanonicalEncodingError. Sections 2 and 5 say NaN is invalid everywhere and all errors derive from GieError. Not reachable through Evidence, whose fields are checked first, but reachable by any caller computing the id before building a record.

defects_found.description: The lock hash is computed over Path.read_text() output, which applies universal-newline translation, not over the file bytes. A released schema whose bytes changed only in line endings (LF -> CRLF, e.g. an autocrlf checkout) is not reported by check(), while any external SHA-256 of the file no longer matches LOCK.json. By the same mechanism write() would emit CRLF files on Windows whose byte hash differs from the lock; that part could not be tested on Linux.

defects_found.description: behaviour() puts the module-level IDENTITY_RULES[name] dict itself into its result, so json_schema(cls)['x-gie-behaviour']['identity'] aliases global state. reports.summary:
Wrote the four S00-ACC-02 test modules (185 test functions, 2193 parametrised cases): 2180 pass, 13 are left failing on purpose and map to 8 defects. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on all four files, and the result is the same in either file order. Nothing under gie/, specifications/, docs/, tools/, conftest or samples.py was touched; `tests/gie/contracts/__init__.py` already existed and was left alone.

The two findings I would look at first:
- **Evolution check rejects the documented way to add a field.** An optional field declared with `fld(Opt(...), since=(1, 1))` makes the generator emit `x-gie-since`, which `classify_schema_change` treats as MAJOR. The first legitimate 1.1.0 of any contract would fail `schema_gen --check`.
- **Same-instant request and report sort backwards.** A broker report with the same receive instant as its request gets rank 20 against the request's 80, so `ordering_key` puts seq 1 before seq 0 in one stream and `merge_ordered` raises `OutOfOrderError`. The ledger and `MemoryJournal` both accept that sequence as valid.

The other six are minor:
- a new `mode`/`venue` field carrying LIVE is classified MINOR (the independent vocabulary check in `schema_gen.check()` still catches it);
- `broker_order_id` is not verified by `OrderEvent`;
- `market_event_id` leaks `decimal.InvalidOperation` / `TypeError` for NaN prices;
- the lock hash ignores line-ending changes;
- `json_schema()` hands out the module-level identity-rule dict, so editing a returned schema changes later output;
- the sample fixture has a stop request timestamped 1 ms before the fill it reacts to. This one is in `tests/gie/samples.py`, not in the code under test.

One spec gap has no failing test: section 4 does not say that a decimal identity part is hashed as `{"d": "..."}`; I pinned `market_event_id` using the form the code and `tests/gie/core/test_ids.py` use.

Coverage by file:
- **`test_compatibility.py`**: section 8 reader rules on real messages for all ten contracts, including the older-MINOR case and the since-version rule; `classify_schema_change` on deep copies of the generated schemas (about 85 MAJOR mutations, each with a reason); every edit of the mode/venue vocabulary; `check_evolution`, `declared_change`, `can_read`; three COM-06 checks.
- **`test_schema_lock.py`**: repository consistency and CLI; the committed lock; schema structure and JSON Schema 2020-12 validity; all 49 sample variants validated against the published schemas; published behaviour and transition tables against the code tables and `FIELDS.md`; `check()` and `write()` on damaged temporary copies, including APPROVED refusal and version-bump scenarios; the `FIELDS.md` check.
- **`test_identity.py`**: all 16 identity functions for form, determinism, per-part sensitivity and about 470 invalid-input cases; pinned values computed with `hashlib` over hand-written payloads; the semantic rules of section 4; records refusing foreign identifiers.
- **`test_contract_ordering.py`**: the section 6.1 table parsed from the specification and compared with `STREAMS`; stream name, ordering time and key for every sample variant; both `OrderEvent` ranks for all 13 event types; same-instant causal sorting; unknown record types.

defects_found.description: Round-trip break (S00-ACC-01) in Float.decode, together with the integer rendering in gie/core/canonical.py. A float field holding an integer-valued double strictly between 2**53 and 2**63 is written with the ECMAScript shortest-digits rule, e.g. the double 1234567890123456768 becomes the literal 1234567890123456800. That literal is inside the 64-bit range, so strict_loads returns an int, and Float.decode refuses it because float(int) != int. A valid record can therefore be constructed and encoded to canonical bytes but not decoded again. Affected are all unbounded float fields (NamedValue.value in Evidence.features and ModelVersion.metrics, Contribution.weight_r, expected_net_r, baseline_r, QuantilePoint.value_r and others). Values up to 2**53 and from 2**63 on round-trip correctly. SHARED_CONTRACTS.md section 7 only states the rule for literals beyond 64 bits; the case inside 64 bits is unspecified and the implementation is inconsistent between writer and reader.
defects_found.reproducer:
from gie.contracts import NamedValue, from_json, to_json
from tests.gie import samples
r = samples.evidence(features=(NamedValue(name='sweep_depth', value=1.2345678901234568e18),))
text = to_json(r)   # contains "value":1234567890123456800
from_json(text)     # ContractValidationError: features[0].value: integer is not exactly representable as a double
defects_found.resolution_note: corrected in the second rework (reviews/session_00/rework_2_change_notice.md); the tests that documented it pass in the gate run

defects_found.description: object_schema lists only non-nullable fields under 'required', so the published JSON Schemas accept a message that omits an optional key. Section 7 says a key missing from a message whose version already has the field is an error, and the decoder refuses it. Key presence is not among the schema limitations listed in section 7, and JSON Schema can express it, so the machine-readable form disagrees with the prose and the reference implementation for every contract with optional fields. A writer in another language that validates against the schema could emit messages the Python reader rejects.

from_wire(w)   # ContractValidationError: bid_volume: field is missing (optional fields are written as explicit null)

defects_found.description: Record.__post_init__ converts only TypeError, ValueError and ArithmeticError from an invariant into ContractValidationError. Its own comment promises that a rule which cannot be evaluated is treated as violated with a contract error. An invariant that reads an attribute of a null optional value (AttributeError), the first element of an empty list (IndexError) or a missing key (KeyError) escapes as a raw Python exception. Latent only: fuzzing every field of all 49 sample variants and every wire path found no shipped invariant that triggers it.

defects_found.description: to_wire, to_json, to_bytes and fingerprint read type(value).CONTRACT without checking that the argument is a Record. Anything that is not a record (None, a dict, a str, a contract class, a list of records) is refused with a raw AttributeError instead of a GieError, although section 5 says all errors derive from GieError and only exact registered classes are accepted anywhere. Subclasses, look-alikes and nested records are correctly refused with UnknownContractError.

defects_found.description: check() does not verify that a golden file's envelope matches its <Contract>-<version> directory. In a directory that is not the current version, any file that merely decodes is accepted, so a message of another contract or version can sit there unnoticed and the compatibility evidence for that released version becomes vacuous. In a current-version directory such a file is reported only indirectly ('has no sample variant' or bytes differ).

defects_found.description: Observation, no failing test left for it: Record.__init_subclass__ decides from cls.__module__ alone whether a record may be defined. A class body or type() call anywhere can set __module__ to 'gie.contracts.<anything>' (or 'tests.<anything>') and is then accepted, and can be registered with registry.contract() as a new top-level contract. The sentence in section 1 ('the framework refuses a contract class defined outside gie.contracts') therefore holds only for classes that do not claim another module name. Existing contracts cannot be replaced this way, because duplicate names are refused and to_wire checks the exact registered class.

limitations: The rule that Record subclasses cannot be defined outside gie.contracts was verified only through the claimed __module__ (type(...) with a module name) from a tests.* module; behaviour inside a real subsystem package could not be exercised.

FieldSpec.since semantics were tested with test-local synthetic records (decode_fields with DecodeContext, and the full codec path via a monkeypatched copy of the private registry dict registry._CONTRACTS). No real contract has a field added after 1.0, so nothing could be tested on real contracts.
Tolerant decoding of a newer MINOR on real contracts was tested with Evidence only (plus the synthetic contract); the other nine rely on the shared code path.

Hypothesis mutations start from the sample builders: the TradePlan and OrderEvent properties generate only BUY limit entries (OrderEvent only SUBMIT_REQUESTED), Position only open GIE BUY positions, RiskDecision only APPROVED_REDUCED in NORMAL state. Other shapes (SELL, fills, closed/external positions, profit protection, unscored candidates) are covered by the 49 sample variants and the generic properties, not by generated values.
All generated and mutated records keep DataOrigin.SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE; BROKER_FEED and HISTORICAL origins were deliberately never constructed, so their round trip is not tested.

The cross-check against FIELDS.md covers field names and nullability per contract; the type and unit columns were not parsed and compared field by field (JSON types are checked through the framework's field specs).

The per-field 'fingerprint differs' test varies 5 to 28 fields per contract with single-field mutations plus a handful of builder-based pairs; fields bound to identifiers that the builders cannot vary in isolation are not all covered.

make_golden.write() was tested on temporary copies only. The branch that refuses --force after owner approval could not be exercised because the schema lock is PROPOSED; the test asserts whichever branch matches the current lock status.
Bypassing immutability with object.__setattr__, pickle or copy was not tested (only normal attribute assignment, deletion and dataclasses.replace).

The four test files for S00-ACC-01 and the contract framework are written: 1391 tests pass and 8 are left failing on purpose, each pointing at a defect described below. Ruff check and format pass on all four files; the run is deterministic and takes about 37 s.

The one finding that matters for the acceptance test is a real round-trip break: a float field holding an integer-valued double strictly between 2**53 and 2**63 is written by `to_json` as an integer literal that `from_json` then refuses. Any `NamedValue` feature or metric with such a value (for example a nanosecond instant stored as a float) produces a record that can be written but not read back. The other failing tests cover four minor gaps (see `defects_found`).

What the files cover:
- **`test_roundtrip.py`** (53 test functions): round trip for all ten contracts and all 49 sample variants, envelope and explicit nulls checked against FIELDS.md, JSON Schema validation (generated and committed), strict decoding at every nesting level with full error paths, version rules, refusal of subclasses and look-alikes, and fingerprint behaviour including idempotent duplicates.
- **`test_roundtrip_property.py`** (17): one hypothesis property per contract plus generic properties over all variants for null toggling, shuffled canonical lists, trailing-zero decimals and floats.
- **`test_spec_framework.py`** (38): every field type on construction and decoding using test-local synthetic records, invariants, frozen/hashable/equality, `fld`/`record` rules, `FieldSpec.since` semantics, registry and semver, where records may be defined, and `object_schema`.
- **`test_golden.py`** (18): committed golden files decode, re-encode byte for byte and validate against the schema of their version; tampering on a `tmp_path` copy is detected; `write()` behaviour.

The `since` tests through the codec register a synthetic contract in a monkeypatched copy of the registry's private `_CONTRACTS` dict, so nothing leaks into other tests; no real contract name is used with `@contract`.

No file outside the four test files was changed; `tests/gie/contracts/__init__.py` already existed (empty).

This contradicts the docstring of _clamped_ns ('Only the first and the last representable trading day are affected') and SHARED_CONTRACTS section 5 rule 2 (invalid input is never clamped). The messages of require_fresh / require_not_expired are built from caller text (what=...), so this is reachable through gie.core.freshness. limitations: The value of parameters_sha256 for the real file is not pinned as a literal: the hash formula is not normative anywhere outside the code, so only its documented properties are tested (format, reproducibility, sensitivity to value/kind/name, stability otherwise, equality with an independently written file of the same nine numbers).

Refusal tests for the parameter loader check the reason through keywords of the message (for example 'range', 'kind', 'required', 'unknown', 'fraction', 'decimal') and through the parameter or key name being mentioned. The specification does not fix message texts, so a rewording of messages would need test maintenance; this was accepted to keep the tests from passing vacuously.

Canonical JSON underflow: literals that round to a non-zero subnormal with a large relative error (for example 3e-324, which becomes 5e-324) are asserted neither way, because the specification only names literals that become zero.

The failing tests for integers of more than 4300 digits (5 node ids in test_errors, test_freshness and test_params) depend on CPython's default integer-string limit; with the limit disabled they would pass.
The clock-mode defect is demonstrated with a test double whose `mode` is not a ClockMode member; no conforming Clock implementation in the repository triggers it.

Not covered: non-Clock objects passed as `clock` (AttributeError), a non-string `what`, ResearchParameters.get with an unhashable name (observed to raise TypeError; neither tested nor reported as a defect), direct construction of ResearchParameters with unvalidated content, and gie.contracts.identity.opportunity_id (belongs to the contracts suites).

The work took longer than the 25-minute time box, mainly because test_params.py had to be rewritten rather than patched.

reports.summary:
Maintained and extended the six gie/core suites against the hardened code. Result: 2022 passed, 21 failed; every remaining failure is a reported defect (8 defects, 1 major, 7 minor). Ruff check and format check pass on all six files. Each file gives the same result run alone or together, and two consecutive runs gave identical outcomes.

What changed per file:
- test_params.py: rewritten for the strict loader (old synthetic fixture had no `kind` and no required parameters, so its defect tests would have passed vacuously). New synthetic file carries the nine required parameters plus one extra of each kind; every defect test changes exactly one thing. Covers the three kinds with boundaries, percent-typed-as-fraction ("-3" for "-0.03"), unknown top-level and parameter keys, each required parameter missing / misspelt / wrong kind, 28 wrong orderings of the daily levels with boundaries, and `parameters_sha256` (changes on any value, kind, name, add/remove; stable on reorder, comments, CRLF, reworded text, equivalent spellings). The real-file checks against MASTER.txt are kept and now also check kinds and REQUIRED_PARAMETERS.
- test_errors.py and test_freshness.py: the interrupted engineer's work was correct and is kept; I fixed its 8 lint errors and added tests (detail names, values with unusable repr, enum scalars, invalid clock readings in both modes, paper clock stepped backwards, keyword-only signatures, unknown clock mode).
- test_timeutil.py: clamped bounds of 1970-01-01 and 2262-04-12, an independent oracle for both limits, a property over all instants, and out-of-range days.
- test_ids.py: `opp` prefix, register exactly equal to the 14 documented prefixes and to FIELDS.md, two pinned `opp` identifiers computed with sha256sum.
- test_canonical.py: 18 underflowing literals refused (text, bytes, nested), every spelling of zero and the smallest doubles still accepted, two properties.

Decisions on the originally failing tests: all were documented behaviour changes and were rewritten at the same or higher strictness (17 to 18 error types, tolerance bounded to one second, typed parameters). No test was weakened; the only deleted test (`9999-12-31` bounds) lives on as a case of the new out-of-range test.

The one major defect: `trading_day_bounds_ns` clamps every out-of-range day, not just the first and last, so "1969-12-31" returns (0, 0) and "2300-01-01" returns (MAX, MAX) instead of being refused.

defects_found.description: SystemClock.regressions_observed misses backward steps that happen while the wall source is still behind. The docstrings say "each backward step is counted once" and "how often the underlying time source was seen to step backwards", but now_ns() only counts the transition into the behind state (the _behind flag). After a backward step the wall source never catches up on its own, because both scales run at the same pace; it only catches up if the wall clock is stepped forward. So in practice the counter stays at 1 for the rest of the run however many further backward steps occur, and health monitoring that watches for increments sees nothing. The now_ns() values themselves are correct.

A float or Decimal capacity is accepted and record() then raises TypeError (list indices must be integers) once the window is full. defects_found.description: RoutingGuard is not actually final. __init_subclass__ raises only after type.__new__ has already created the subclass, so the subclass object exists; it is reachable through RoutingGuard.__subclasses__() or the exception's traceback, and it can be instantiated. The result is an object that passes isinstance(x, RoutingGuard), has a genuine mode and carries overridden authorize / authorized_methods that admit anything. Mitigation in place today: gie.contracts.guarded.GuardedExecutionAdapter requires type(guard) is RoutingGuard and calls RoutingGuard.authorized_methods unbound, so the official gateway is not fooled; any other consumer that duck-types or uses isinstance would be. Because the bypass needs deliberate code and the gateway holds, this could reasonably be downgraded to minor. A possible fix is to refuse in __init__ when type(self) is not RoutingGuard, or to refuse in a metaclass before the class is created.

reports.summary:
The four core test suites are updated to the hardened, documented behaviour: 1042 tests pass and 14 are left failing, each one a reported defect in the code under test. Ruff check and format pass on all four files; nothing outside them was edited.

What changed per file:
- **`test_clock.py` (257 tests):** the SystemClock section is rewritten for "never decreases and never stands still". New tests cover the `regressions_observed` property, the Scheduler protocol, `ReplayClock.call_after`, and PollingScheduler. Two replay/paper equivalence properties are added: the same schedule script on both, and a run loop with inputs where the paper loop polls late. Every test that involves ReplayClock carries `S00-ACC-03`.
- **`test_ordering.py` (239 tests):** the new StreamRank members, order and specification rank numbers; `first_seq` default 0 and `None`; constructor and `observe` argument validation; the ordering-time rule; `restore()`. The reference-model property test now includes ordering time.
- **`test_latency.py` (131 tests):** unchanged behaviour, so only two tests were added (capacity type, and `measure()` using only `perf_counter_ns`).
- **`test_routing_lock.py` (429 tests):** rewritten. Module-level `pytestmark` applies the five requirement ids and `S00-ACC-04` to every test (checked with `--gie-evidence`). Helper adapters satisfy the new rules, and the registry dict is snapshotted and restored per test. All the documented lock rules in the task are covered.

The 14 failures correspond to seven defects (nine are listed in `defects_found`; two have no failing test):
- **Major:** SystemClock misses backward steps after the first one, and a refused RoutingGuard subclass can still be instantiated and used as a permissive guard.
- **Minor:** `PollingScheduler.call_after` clamps where replay refuses; `restore()` raises `TypeError` on mixed-type keys; `LatencyRecorder` does not validate capacity type; registering an impersonating class corrupts the genuine class's registry entry; the self-check raises `KeyError` for one kind of enum tampering.

`tests/gie/core/test_ordering.py` no longer shows as modified because another process made snapshot commits during the session that included it; I ran no state-changing git commands.

reports.summary:
Wrote six independent test modules (858 tests, parametrised) for the model registry contract, the Clock and run contracts, the journal, the derivation rules and the service interfaces. 842 pass; 16 are left failing on purpose because the implementation (or, in one case, the sample fixture) contradicts the specification. ruff check and ruff format --check pass on all seven files. Adding these files does not change the outcome of any other test in tests/gie (compared with and without them).

Coverage against the task:
- ModelVersion: every invariant MDL-1..9 has accepted and rejected cases, both constructed and decoded, asserting details['invariant']. All 42 status pairs are run through validate_model_transition against the FIELDS.md table. Also covered: immutable artifact fields, revision +1, strictly increasing status time, rollback_of exactly on re-activation, approver and D-nnn patterns, `validated`, revision floors, and is_out_of_sample boundaries. validate_registry_history covers promotion, rollback with new versus reused approval, two ACTIVE versions, wrong replaces, seq gaps and composites.
- Clock: CLK-1..3 accepted and rejected (constructed and decoded), Prague-midnight boundaries, read_clock with ReplayClock and with a SystemClock on scripted fake sources (regressions propagated, mode pairing).
- RunManifest / RunContext: RUN-1..4 accepted and rejected (constructed and decoded), LIVE not constructible, not decodable and not derivable as a run id; RunContext refuses the wrong clock kind and a differing parameter hash.
- Journal: manifest first, other run or mode refused, idempotent publish, conflicts, gaps, counted tick gaps, decreasing ordering time, refused records leaving entries, streams, ledger and file unchanged, lifecycle rules through the ledger, the look-ahead guard, read() and streams(), and replay determinism. FileJournal: canonical lines, reopen and continue, re-sent duplicates after restart, torn tail and repair_torn_tail, 33 kinds of modified file, a sampled single-byte substitution check, and close.
- check_derivation: each rule violated separately, a 3x3 origin matrix, the expiry chain, and one hypothesis property (derandomised).
- Interfaces: all nine protocols, structural stand-ins, GuardedExecutionAdapter checked on the class only.

Ten defects are reported below: four major, six minor. The four major ones are the journal's check order, a closed FileJournal keeping a refused record in memory, the ledger not enforcing the family-level model rules of section 9.2, and validate_registry_history accepting a rollback_of from another model family.

Two observations have no failing test because the specification is ambiguous:
- The look-ahead guard is inactive until the first tick has been journaled, so a journal without ticks accepts any watermark.
- The journal comment says registry streams are joined in the middle, but the ledger refuses a model whose first journaled entry is not RESEARCH revision 0.

Two notes on the working tree: a WIP snapshot commit made by someone else picked up these files while I was working (I ran no state-changing git command), and gie/core files were being modified concurrently by others.

defects_found.description: The daily profit floor is forgotten as soon as a decision reports another daily state. validate_daily_state_sequence only compares the floor when BOTH consecutive decisions carry one, and LifecycleLedger keeps only the newest decision per producer. Within one Prague trading day (a) an approval at or below the floor protected earlier that day is accepted once daily_state is reported as NORMAL or DEFENSIVE, because RSK-7 cannot see a floor that is no longer on the record, and (b) the floor can be lowered through an intermediate decision without floor. This contradicts SHARED_CONTRACTS 9.2 ('Within a trading day ... the profit floor never decreases', enforced by the ledger) and owner spec G05-06 / G05-08. The same gap also affects gie/contracts/ledger.py.

defects_found.description: GuardedExecutionAdapter authorises a request against whatever Position / TradePlan object the caller passes and never compares it with the newest record of that chain in the run's LifecycleLedger, which it holds. A snapshot that the ledger already knows to be outdated therefore authorises an order that does not 'only reduce' the position: an EXIT for the old volume after a partial close, or after the position was CLOSED, reaches the adapter and would open opposite exposure without plan, approval or stop. Likewise an entry is sent for the SELECTED revision of a plan whose WITHDRAWN revision is already in the ledger. This contradicts 9.3 ('every other order needs the open GIE position it belongs to and may only reduce it ... volume not above the open volume'; 'an entry needs its SELECTED plan'). The finding rests on reading 'the open position' and 'its SELECTED plan' as the current state known to the run's ledger; the coordinator should confirm that reading.

defects_found.description: feed_silence_ns(last_tick, now_ns) does not validate now_ns as an instant. SHARED_CONTRACTS section 2 defines an instant as an int of nanoseconds in 0..2^63-1, section 5 says invalid input is rejected with ContractValidationError and never coerced, and section 3.3 says a reference instant later than now raises FutureDataError. The sibling helpers in gie/core/freshness.py enforce exactly this (_require_instant); feed_silence_ns, the freshness reference for market data, does not. A float now_ns is compared after rounding to a multiple of 256 ns, so a tick received up to about 128 ns after now can be reported as not in the future (fail-open on look-ahead). bool and out-of-range integers are also accepted, and a non-Tick argument raises AttributeError. Reaching this needs a caller that passes a non-int, which mypy --strict on gie/ would normally catch.

limitations: Windows-only branches were never executed; they are covered only by `mypy --strict --platform win32`, AST checks and fakes. This applies to: the shared-read `CreateFileW` opener (it falls back to a plain open on any error), extended-length `\\?\` paths on a real volume, junction and cloud-placeholder detection on real NTFS, `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`, the registry lookup of the CPU name, the real `tasklist` / `schtasks` processes (OEM code-page decoding, localised column names, exit codes), the Windows string form of the `subprocess.Popen` audit event (tested by calling the guard handler directly), and Windows last-access-time behaviour.

No Python 3.8, 3.9 or 3.10 interpreter is available. Compatibility with 3.8 is checked statically (`ast.parse(feature_version=(3, 8))` plus AST checks for match statements, parenthesised with, runtime-subscripted builtins, `X | None` and a list of newer attributes); the tool was only run on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13.

`manifest.jsonl` has no `tool` block: it contains file records only, so that two runs are byte-identical and the format matches the `manifest` sub-command. The tool block is in `inventory.json` and `processes.json`.

Inventory lists are cut at `--max-list-entries` (default 5000) and source files are keyword-scanned up to `--max-scan-bytes` (default 8 MiB); both cuts are recorded in `exclusions_and_caps`. `manifest.jsonl` is never cut.

Secret-looking files are recognised by name or directory only. An ordinary file that contains a credential (for example config.py) is hashed and its SHA-256 is in the manifest; the credential scan reports the location and the README tells the owner what to review.
The column-name heuristic can still emit a headerless first line that consists only of word-like fields. The README asks the owner to check, and `--no-csv-headers` disables headers.
Excluded directories are only counted (files, bytes), so `compare` cannot see changes inside them unless `--no-default-excludes --include-venvs` is used. Symlink targets are recorded but not hashed.

Process inventory: relevance is decided by image-name patterns. On Linux only `/proc` (name, pid, resident memory) is read; cron and systemd timers are not collected. On Windows, scheduled tasks under `\Microsoft\` are only counted.

Depending on the Python version, the standard library's `platform.platform()` (required by the task) may itself run a helper once (`ver` on Windows, `uname -p` on POSIX). It is called before the guard is activated and is documented in the README.
Access times: `O_NOATIME` is used on Linux when permitted, and the access-time test is not acceptance-marked. On Windows, last-access updates depend on a system setting and are not controlled.
`write_manifest` never overwrites an existing file. If `tools/baseline_freeze.py` needs to replace a manifest, it must remove or rename the old file itself.

`tools.check_no_secrets` and `tools.check_live_lock` did not exist yet, so my files were not run against them. The tool and its tests necessarily contain broker keywords (MetaTrader5, order_send, OrderSend) and credential-shaped fixture text. Every such fixture value contains the literal `FAKE-NOT-A-SECRET`, but those scanners may need an allowlist for `tools/audit/` and `tests/gie/tools/test_baseline_audit.py`.
The audit of `D:\ftmo_eurusd` itself is still not performed (blocker B-001); this delivery is the tool, not the audit result.

- Files are opened through one function with mode `rb`; outputs are created through one function with mode `xb`, so nothing can be overwritten.
- While a tree is scanned, an interpreter audit hook blocks any write, rename, delete, chmod, utime or chdir under the root, any network use, and any process start other than the two fixed `tasklist` / `schtasks` queries.
- The tool refuses (exit 2) when `--out` overlaps `--root`, when `--out` is non-empty, and when the tool, its interpreter or a loaded module lives inside `--root`.

**Verification**
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy --strict` and `mypy --strict --platform win32` pass on the tool; the tests also pass with the CI flags (`--cov`, `--gie-evidence`, `--junitxml`) and in reverse order.

- A whole-suite run in the shared tree showed failures in other engineers' areas (routing lock, timeutil, compatibility); they fail without my files too.

**API notes for `tools/baseline_freeze.py`**
- `build_manifest(root, includes=None, *, excluded_dirs=None, detect_environments=True, hash_sensitive=False, max_hash_bytes=None, progress_every=0)` returns records sorted by path with `path`, `size`, `mtime_ns`, `sha256` (or `None` plus `skipped`).

- `compare_manifests(a, b, strict_mtime=False)` accepts record lists or file paths and returns `added`, `removed`, `changed`, `mtime_only`, `unverified`, `content_identical` and `exit_code`.

- Directories containing `pyvenv.cfg` or `conda-meta` are excluded and summarised like the default names; `--include-venvs` turns this off.

- Cloud "online-only" placeholder files are listed but not read.
- In `compare`, a file without a hash counts as changed if its size or mtime moved, otherwise it is listed as `unverified`.

If the run loop has already begun a step later than that timer's due time, begin_step raises ClockRegressionError. Raising is correct (fail closed), but the timer is gone: it never fires, pending_timers() is 0 and next_timer_ns() is None. A refused poll silently loses a timer such as a feed-silence check or an expiry, whereas a refusal should change nothing (the ReplayClock rule: on failure 'all other timers stay pending'). The paper fixtures are now PaperClock(SystemClock on a fake time source) + PollingScheduler, and the paper run loop is pass time -> run_due(limit) -> begin_step. Old rules that changed were rewritten with the same boundary values and asserting the new rule:
- 'a past due time is not an error' became two tests: a due time before the step instant is refused, exactly as in ReplayClock (ClockRegressionError); a due time between the step instant and the wall clock fires at the next poll.
- call_after is now relative to the step instant.
- Callbacks now see now_ns == due time; the wall clock (wall_ns) still shows the real, later time.
- The nested-scheduling test now expects the refusal of a timer scheduled before the callback's own due time.
- The 'any Clock can drive it' test now drives a PaperClock on a fake source, with the operating-system time functions replaced by functions that fail.
- The replay/paper equivalence properties are stricter: the instant seen inside every callback and at every input must be equal in both modes.

New clock tests:
- PaperClock: the clock protocol and SYSTEM mode; step time does not move between begin_step calls while wall_ns and monotonic_ns do; begin_step boundaries (the current instant and the wall reading are accepted, one less is ClockRegressionError, one more is FutureDataError, non-instants are ContractValidationError); it runs only on a system clock; regressions_observed is passed through and is read-only.
- PollingScheduler: it accepts only an exact PaperClock (a system clock, a replay clock, a view, a subclass, None or object() are refused); run_due begins a step at each due time; a timer a callback registers for its own instant fires in the same run_due; step time stays at a failed timer's instant.
- ClockView / SchedulerView: the exact public surface (no advance_to, advance_by, begin_step, run_due or wall_ns); nothing can be set on them; each wraps exactly one clock or scheduler (a view of a view behaves the same).

- Registration is accepted when the class, the registering code and the method globals all live in an allowed module. It is refused for a spoofed __module__ whose methods live elsewhere, for a single foreign method, and for a registering module outside the allow-list.
- After registration, a change to a method's __code__, __defaults__ or __kwdefaults__ (replaced or changed in place) or to a closure cell is refused by the guard, and re-registering does not launder it; restoring the originals restores admission.
- The self-check detects an alias class attribute (RunMode.LIVE = RunMode.PAPER, ExecutionVenue.LIVE / MT5_DEMO = SIMULATED) and a forged member added as an attribute. defects_found.description: The gateway journals a request before it checks the adapter against the routing lock. submit(), cancel() and replace() call self._journal.publish(event) and only then self._call(...), and _call is where RoutingGuard.authorized_methods(guard, adapter) runs. The module docstring promises the opposite order for every call ('1. authorises the adapter with the RoutingGuard ... 4. publishes the request ... before the adapter sees it'), and so does change notice section 5 ('routing lock -> authorisation -> journal.publish(request) -> adapter'). The lock itself still holds: the modified or unregistered adapter is never called. But the write-ahead journal now holds a request that was never sent and is now part of the run's ledger (an open order). An engine that re-sends what it is unsure about after a restart would send it again.
defects_found.reproducer: In a test module (the lock only accepts registrations from tests or the execution packages): register a simulated adapter class A; journal = MemoryJournal() with samples.run_story()[:6] published; gw = GuardedExecutionAdapter(A(), RoutingGuard('REPLAY'), clock=ReplayClock(T0 + 2 ms), journal=journal); monkeypatch A.submit (or set A.venue = 'LIVE', or delete A.poll); n = len(journal); gw.submit(samples.order_event()) raises LiveRoutingLockedError, but len(journal) == n + 1 and journal.ledger.order(order.client_order_id) is the request (expected: n, and None).

defects_found.description: Undocumented change (the change notice is silent). In poll(), 'except LiveRoutingLockedError: raise' aborts the whole batch when one report belongs to another run mode. This contradicts the PollResult docstring ('Reports behind a refused one are still processed, so nothing that is valid is lost') and change notice section 5 ('a refused report is returned in errors and does not hide the others'). Fail-closed behaviour would be kept either by putting the LiveRoutingLockedError into PollResult.errors, or by documenting that a lock violation aborts the batch.
defects_found.reproducer: rig with the sample entry submitted; a = next event ACCEPTED/WORKING of the entry (seq 1); adapter.reports = [replace(a, mode=PAPER) built via OrderEvent(...), a]; gateway.poll() raises LiveRoutingLockedError, and journal.ledger.order(entry.client_order_id) is still the submit (expected: a journaled, the lock error surfaced).

The 14 failures are two code defects. I left those tests failing on purpose.

1. Major (13 tests): the gateway writes a request to the journal before it checks the adapter against the routing lock. The adapter never receives the request, but the journal now holds a request that was never sent.
2. Minor (1 test): when an adapter returns a report of another run mode, poll() raises. Valid reports in the same batch are then lost, because the adapter has already handed them over.

One more minor point, with no failing test: validate_entry_authorization now refuses an entry request stamped later than the clock reading. The change notice does not mention this rule.

- **tests/gie/contracts/test_order_event.py:** fixed the test builders for the new fields and the broker reason code.
  - The state machine table now has the 4 added PENDING_CANCEL rows (40 rows), and a partial fill is never reconciled back to WORKING.

A broker RECONCILED report that takes the working stop to REJECTED or EXPIRED, while all 0.50 lots are still open by fills, is admitted. limitations: LL015 matches rename/replace by name and by the one-argument Path signature. Any one-argument `.replace(x)` that is not on a gateway-named receiver is reported, including a simulated adapter forwarding `self.book.replace(request)`. This is documented as deliberately not relaxed; narrowing it is a coordinator decision.

LL015 does not see writes made through other libraries (numpy.save, DataFrame.to_csv, zipfile, sqlite3, logging.FileHandler, shelve, dbm), a write method reached through a value the resolution does not follow (`opener = path.open`), or a write in a C extension or subprocess beyond what LL003 already forbids. All of this is documented in the tool's honest limits.

LL015 picks the mode argument of an `open` call by position. The second positional argument is used for a plain name or for an attribute of an imported module or class; otherwise the first. An object imported from another module and opened as `obj.open('w')` is read as a module function, so its first argument is not checked.

AR008 does not see a wrapper that forwards to the plain helpers under another name, or a tolerance passed in `**options`. AR009 does not see plain-name calls such as `submit(...)`, a getattr with a computed name, or names that appear only in string annotations. All documented.
